newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 28 Moslem rebels - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 28 Moslem rebels - newspaper.

text.p: Algerian security forces and pro-government militiamen have killed 28 Moslem rebels, including a suspected bomber shot dead along with two other guerrillas in Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.
Security forces killed three guerrillas in central Algiers on Monday as they were set to carry out assassinations, Liberte newspaper said.

One of the three was identified as Redouane Mouhamer, sought by the authorities for his alleged role in a January 21 car bomb explosion in central Agiers in which at least six people were killed and more than 40 wounded, Liberte said.
A group of 17 guerrillas were killed in an operation last week in Tacheta region, 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Algiers, the paper said, quoting security sources.

Eight more rebels were killed in a gun battle with pro-government anti-Islamist militia known as Patriots in Ain Defla area, 130 km (80 miles) south of the Algerian capital, last week, the newspaper said.
The Liberte report brought to more than 250 the number of people reported killed during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, which began on January 10.
In the latest massacre of civilians reported in Algeria, 31 people were killed by having their heads hacked off with an axe or a knife in a rebel raid in Medea, south of Agiers, on Friday.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
